name: Code Quality & SOLID Principles
when_applicable: Any codebase with production code (not prototypes, scripts, or throwaway code)

criteria.criterion: Each function does exactly one thing — a single, clear responsibility describable in one sentence without 'and'
criteria.how_to_test: Read function bodies — flag functions that do input validation AND business logic AND persistence. Each should be split.

criteria.criterion: Each class has a single reason to change — one responsibility, one actor it serves
criteria.how_to_test: Check class methods — if methods serve different concerns (e.g., UserService with authenticate(), sendEmail(), generateReport()), flag it.

criteria.criterion: New behavior is added via extension (new classes, plugins, strategies), not by modifying existing working code
criteria.how_to_test: Look for if/elif/switch chains that grow with new features. These should be polymorphism, strategy pattern, or registries instead.

criteria.criterion: Subtypes are substitutable for their base types without breaking behavior — no TypeError surprises
criteria.how_to_test: Check inheritance hierarchies — subclasses should not raise NotImplementedError for base methods or violate base class contracts.

criteria.criterion: Interfaces are client-specific and small — no god-interfaces that force implementors to stub methods they don't use
criteria.how_to_test: Find interfaces/protocols with 6+ methods. Check if all implementors actually use every method. Flag pass/NotImplementedError stubs.

criteria.criterion: High-level modules depend on abstractions, not concrete low-level implementations
criteria.how_to_test: Check constructor parameters — high-level business logic should receive interfaces, not concrete DB/HTTP/file classes.

criteria.criterion: Functions are under 50 lines (ideally under 20). No function exceeds 50 lines without strong justification.
criteria.how_to_test: Count lines per function. Flag any over 30 lines, fail any over 50 lines.

criteria.criterion: Files are under 300 lines (ideally under 200). No file exceeds 300 lines.
criteria.how_to_test: Count lines per file (excluding blank lines and imports). Flag any over 200, fail any over 300.

criteria.criterion: No function has cyclomatic complexity above 10 (count decision points: if, elif, for, while, and, or, except)
criteria.how_to_test: Count branches per function. Flag functions with 7+ decision points, fail at 10+.

criteria.criterion: No code nests deeper than 3 levels of indentation (use early returns, guard clauses, extraction)
criteria.how_to_test: Check indentation levels — flag any code at 4+ levels deep. Suggest early returns or function extraction.

criteria.criterion: Variables, functions, and classes reveal their purpose — no single-letter names (except loop counters), no abbreviations unless universal
criteria.how_to_test: Scan for names like 'x', 'tmp', 'data', 'info', 'mgr', 'proc'. Flag unclear/ambiguous names.

criteria.criterion: Consistent naming conventions across the codebase — same concept uses the same name everywhere
criteria.how_to_test: Check for inconsistencies: 'user' vs 'customer' vs 'account' for the same concept, 'get' vs 'fetch' vs 'retrieve' for the same operation.

criteria.criterion: No substantial logic duplicated across multiple locations — shared logic is extracted into reusable functions
criteria.how_to_test: Search for near-identical code blocks (3+ lines repeated in 2+ places). Flag copy-paste with minor variations.

criteria.criterion: Configuration, constants, and business rules have a single source of truth — not scattered across files
criteria.how_to_test: Check for magic numbers, duplicated string constants, or the same business rule implemented in multiple places.

criteria.criterion: Modules have low coupling — changing one module does not require cascading changes across unrelated modules
criteria.how_to_test: Check import graphs — flag modules with 8+ imports from different modules, or circular import chains.

criteria.criterion: Classes and modules have high cohesion — all methods/functions within relate to the same responsibility
criteria.how_to_test: Check if all methods in a class use the same instance variables. Flag classes where methods split into unrelated groups.

criteria.criterion: Errors are handled explicitly — no bare except/catch-all, no swallowed exceptions, no silent failures
criteria.how_to_test: Find try/except or try/catch blocks. Flag bare 'except:', 'except Exception:', or empty catch blocks. Errors should be logged or re-raised.

criteria.criterion: Error handling happens at boundaries (API layer, I/O), not scattered through business logic
criteria.how_to_test: Check domain/application layer for try/except blocks. Business logic should raise domain exceptions; boundaries catch and translate them.

criteria.criterion: Type hints/annotations are used for function signatures and complex data structures — no 'any' types without justification
criteria.how_to_test: Check function signatures — flag missing type hints on public functions. Flag use of Any/any/Object without a comment explaining why.

criteria.criterion: Critical business logic has test coverage — happy path + at least 2 edge cases per critical function
criteria.how_to_test: Identify core business functions. Check for corresponding test files. Flag untested critical paths.
